mutants.label: A: delete the advisory bullet (reader-born REASONED finding is advisory)
mutants.find: - **Advisory.** A REASONED finding whose target is a reader-born rule or its boundary is advisory: it never blocks, never gets a new criterion, and its default is an [outside-this-contract line](#subtract-first). This covers policy forks (detector 7), unenforced rules (detector 11) and survivors (detector 3), not only input-value mutants.

mutants.label: B: delete the standing-delegation bullet
mutants.find: - **Standing delegation (Charles's decision, 2026-10-03).** The conductor applies Subtract itself, with no approval for the Subtract itself. It deletes each reader-born rule that a blocking or advisory rule-born finding rests on, rewrites each case as an outside-this-contract line, and lists every deletion and added line in the REWRITE comment under a `Subtracted (veto within the next read)` heading. Charles's silence is assent, and he may veto by name. A deletion of a traced rule is never delegated. It does not reset the read count, so the cap in step 8 still binds and still sends the slice to Charles.

mutants.label: C: delete the read-2 trigger bullet
mutants.find: - **Trigger.** Subtract runs from the second fresh read on, on any rule-born finding, and no longer waits for the cap. Rule-born origin is computed by the conductor from the previous REWRITE comment's reader-born list, never self-reported by the reader. (Precedent: afk-app#1-#4 had 8 cap events needing Charles, 7 chose Subtract, and the one Grow, #4, never converged.)

mutants.label: D: delete the empty-repo probe-builds bullet
mutants.find: - **Empty repo (no fork point).** When the target has no commits on the integration target, there is nothing to archive. The digest says `no fork point: probe builds unavailable`. Detectors 3, 9 and 11 mutants are REASONED, and so advisory under the [evidence rule](#evidence-rule) unless traced, and the stamp's `target=` names only whatever `--repo-dir` and `--target` were passed (the stamp regex needs a branch and a SHA, so it cannot say `none`) and certifies nothing about the empty repo. Prefer sequencing: when slices depend on a foundation slice that builds the tree, read the foundation slice first and the siblings only after it has landed, so their reads get a fork point and real probe builds. The digest names this option. (Precedent: afk-app#1-#4 ran on an empty repo, so every detector 3, 9 and 11 mutant was REASONED and reachability failed closed on all of them; [the-workshop#1105](https://github.com/cdcoonce/the-workshop/issues/1105).)

mutants.label: E: delete the conductor-counts-the-cap sentences from step 8
mutants.find: The conductor counts the cap, never the reader. Count fresh reads since the last body Charles approved, from the comment history and the stamp record. A delegated Subtract does not reset the count; only a body Charles approved does. A cap ruling from Charles (Grow, or his by-name acceptance of the applied Subtract) counts as approving that body and restarts the count at 0; silence does not. `read=` in the ledger line, the Evidence rule's 'second fresh read' and the Hand-built tier's 'read 2' count every fresh read on the slice; only the cap count restarts. (Precedent: afk#1548 ran six fresh reads under a cap of three, because Subtracts after reads 2 and 4 each reset the count and the cap never bound.) The reader prompt carries no read or cap count. A reader that reports a cap is ignored.
